name: open_high_low_5s
author: adapted from aggregated_from_x_indian_traders
thesis: Exploiting stocks that make open=high or open=low on 1-min as strong directional bias due to institutional conviction at open. Inefficiency from retail chasing momentum without confirmation. Persists because most traders ignore volume filter + index alignment; costs kill discretionary versions.
mechanism: Institutional order flow arrives in bursts via algorithmic execution (TWAP/VWAP slicing), creating persistent directional pressure over 30-120 seconds. Retail and smaller participants follow the initial move, extending momentum before liquidity absorbs the flow and the order book rebalances.

indicators.name: open_high_low_flag
indicators.formula: (open == high OR open == low) on first bar

weaknesses: Regime dependency: worthless in ranging sideways opens
Slippage on fast moves: open=high/low often coincides with news spikes
Crowding: extremely popular on X leading to alpha decay in top names
prior_art: Open High Low strategy (classic X thread by @bhaveshp1509)
adaptation_notes: Converted from 1min to 5s bars. Lookback multiplier: 12x. Adaptations: timeframe scaling to 5-second candles; apply to NIFTY/BANKNIFTY index instead of FnO universe; lookback period scaling for 5-second bars. Stop/target calibrated for options point-based exits. Universe narrowed to NIFTY index.
